facts.text: Las Palomas gets its name from the Spanish word for doves, because the area’s cotton‑wood groves and springs were once teeming with them.
Las Palomas was founded in 1856 by Hispanic settlers, becoming one of the earliest communities along the Rio Grande Valley.
In the late 1800s, Las Palomas was a key east‑west gateway through Palomas Gap, drawing miners, travelers, and health seekers to its mineral hot springs.
During Elephant Butte Dam’s construction, workers turned Palomas Hot Springs into a bustling resort with saloons and entertainment, spurring growth in nearby Truth or Consequences.
San Isidro Catholic Church, period homes, and the historic cemetery still stand as silent witnesses to Las Palomas’s once‑bustling frontier past.
Las Palomas first emerged in the mid‑1800s, forged amid Apache raids and frequent floods that displaced earlier Rio Grande settlements.
